from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Prerequisite: The Matrix as a Movement"
        lines = [
            '1. Think of a matrix as space in motion.',
            '2. Matrix A transforms the Robot.',
            '3. Columns track basis vectors i and j.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_GRID = "#555555"
        COLOR_ROBOT = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_MATRIX = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_J = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_GRID)
        
        # Define the coordinate system and area
        plane_center = (self.grid["B2"] + self.grid["E4"]) / 2
        coord_sys = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_GRID, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": WHITE, "include_tip": True}
        ).move_to(plane_center)

        # Robot representation
        robot_body = Square(side_length=0.3, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_ROBOT, stroke_width=1)
        robot_eyes = VGroup(
            Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).move_to(robot_body.get_center() + [0.06, 0.06, 0]),
            Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).move_to(robot_body.get_center() + [-0.06, 0.06, 0])
        )
        robot = VGroup(robot_body, robot_eyes)
        
        # Initial position (1,0) in grid coordinates
        robot.move_to(coord_sys.c2p(1, 0))

        # Basis vectors
        vec_i = Arrow(coord_sys.c2p(0, 0), coord_sys.c2p(1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        vec_j = Arrow(coord_sys.c2p(0, 0), coord_sys.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        label_i = Text("i", color=COLOR_I, font_size=20, slant=ITALIC).next_to(vec_i, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_j = Text("j", color=COLOR_J, font_size=20, slant=ITALIC).next_to(vec_j, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(coord_sys), FadeIn(robot), FadeIn(vec_i, label_i), FadeIn(vec_j, label_j), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_MATRIX)

        # Build Matrix A manually using Text and VGroups
        a_eq = Text("A = ", color=COLOR_MATRIX, font_size=25)
        v0 = Text("0", color=COLOR_MATRIX, font_size=25)
        v1 = Text("-1", color=COLOR_MATRIX, font_size=25)
        v2 = Text("1", color=COLOR_MATRIX, font_size=25)
        v3 = Text("0", color=COLOR_MATRIX, font_size=25)
        
        mat_vals = VGroup(v0, v1, v2, v3).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.3)
        bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=40, color=COLOR_MATRIX).next_to(mat_vals, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=40, color=COLOR_MATRIX).next_to(mat_vals, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        matrix_a = VGroup(a_eq, bracket_l, mat_vals, bracket_r).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "B5")
        
        self.play(Write(matrix_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Transformation: A rotation of 90 degrees CCW
        # i(1,0) -> (0,1)
        # j(0,1) -> (-1,0)
        new_vec_i = Arrow(coord_sys.c2p(0, 0), coord_sys.c2p(0, 1), buff=0, color=COLOR_I, stroke_width=4)
        new_vec_j = Arrow(coord_sys.c2p(0, 0), coord_sys.c2p(-1, 0), buff=0, color=COLOR_J, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(vec_i, new_vec_i),
            Transform(vec_j, new_vec_j),
            robot.animate.move_to(coord_sys.c2p(0, 1)),
            label_i.animate.next_to(coord_sys.c2p(0, 1), RIGHT, buff=0.1),
            label_j.animate.next_to(coord_sys.c2p(-1, 0), UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Sequential Challenge"
        lines = [
            "Let's restart our Robot at its original position.",
            "First, Matrix A rotates the Robot ninety degrees.",
            "Now, we introduce Matrix B to add a shear.",
            "Matrix B shifts the Robot to its final destination.",
            "We can track the full path of this journey."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lines)

        # 2. Define Colors and Assets
        ROBOT_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        GRID_COLOR = "#555555"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        MATRIX_B_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        PATH_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # 3. Create Scene Elements
        # Background Plane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GRID_COLOR, "stroke_width": 2, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GRID_COLOR, "include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Robot Mobject
        robot = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=0.4, color=ROBOT_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5),
            Dot(radius=0.03, color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.08 + LEFT*0.08),
            Dot(radius=0.03, color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.08 + RIGHT*0.08),
            Line(LEFT*0.1, RIGHT*0.1, color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.1)
        )
        # Position Robot at (1,0) relative to plane
        robot.move_to(plane.c2p(1, 0))

        # Matrices
        matrix_a = Text("A = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]", font_size=20)
        matrix_b = Text("B = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]", font_size=20, color=MATRIX_B_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, 'A2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_b, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0)

        # Labels (positioned via grid to meet constraints)
        start_label = Text("(1,0)", font_size=16, color=ROBOT_COLOR)
        mid_label = Text("(0,1)", font_size=16, color=ROBOT_COLOR)
        final_label = Text("(1,1)", font_size=16, color=ROBOT_COLOR)
        
        self.place_at_grid(start_label, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(mid_label, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(final_label, 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)

        # Scene coordinates for path tracking
        origin_abs = plane.c2p(0, 0)
        p_start_abs = plane.c2p(1, 0).copy()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(plane), FadeIn(robot), FadeIn(start_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Apply Rotation
        self.play(
            Rotate(plane, PI/2, about_point=origin_abs),
            Rotate(robot, PI/2, about_point=origin_abs),
            FadeOut(start_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(mid_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Apply Shear Matrix B
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=origin_abs),
            robot.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=origin_abs),
            FadeOut(mid_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(final_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Calculate path points in scene space
        # Rotation 90 deg around origin_abs
        rel_start = p_start_abs - origin_abs
        rel_mid = np.array([-rel_start[1], rel_start[0], 0])
        p_mid_abs = origin_abs + rel_mid
        
        # Shear rel_mid by Matrix B
        rel_final = np.array([rel_mid[0] + rel_mid[1], rel_mid[1], 0])
        p_final_abs = origin_abs + rel_final
        
        # Visualize Path
        radius_val = np.linalg.norm(rel_start)
        arc_path = ArcBetweenPoints(p_start_abs, p_mid_abs, radius=radius_val, stroke_color=PATH_COLOR)
        dashed_arc = DashedVMobject(arc_path)
        shear_path = DashedLine(p_mid_abs, p_final_abs, color=PATH_COLOR)
        
        self.play(Create(dashed_arc))
        self.play(Create(shear_path))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup highlighting
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Background and Title Configuration
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        title = Text("Matrix Multiplication: The Art of Composition", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)

        # 2. Lecture Content (Left Side Layout)
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Linear Transformation Chains",
            "- Order of Composition",
            "- Dot Product Perspectives"
        ]
        
        lecture_group = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) 
            for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
        
        lecture_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        # 3. Matrix Visuals (Right Side Layout)
        def create_text_matrix(values, color=WHITE, bracket_color=WHITE):
            # Create elements using Text instead of MathTex
            grid = VGroup(*[
                VGroup(*[Text(str(item), font_size=24, color=color) for item in row]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
                for row in values
            ]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
            
            # Create brackets using Text
            l_bracket = Text("[", font_size=48, color=bracket_color)
            r_bracket = Text("]", font_size=48, color=bracket_color)
            
            # Position brackets
            l_bracket.stretch_to_fit_height(grid.height + 0.2)
            r_bracket.stretch_to_fit_height(grid.height + 0.2)
            l_bracket.next_to(grid, LEFT, buff=0.2)
            r_bracket.next_to(grid, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
            
            return VGroup(l_bracket, grid, r_bracket)

        matrix_a = create_text_matrix([["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]])
        times_symbol = Text("×", font_size=32)
        matrix_b = create_text_matrix([["e", "f"], ["g", "h"]])
        
        matrix_viz = VGroup(matrix_a, times_symbol, matrix_b).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        matrix_viz.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.0)

        # 4. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_group, shift=RIGHT))
        self.play(Create(matrix_viz))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup colors
        COLOR_A = YELLOW
        COLOR_B = "#58C4DD" # BLUE_B
        COLOR_V = "#83C167" # GREEN_C
        
        self.setup_layout("The Right-to-Left Rule", [
            'In notation, the first action sits on the right.', 
            'Like a conveyor belt, vectors enter from the right.', 
            'Matrix A acts first, then Matrix B follows.'
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Formula: (BA)v - Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        formula = Text("(BA)v", font_size=48)
        formula[1].set_color(COLOR_B) # B
        formula[2].set_color(COLOR_A) # A
        formula[4].set_color(COLOR_V) # v
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Sequential highlighting from right to left: v -> A -> B
        self.play(Indicate(formula[4], color=COLOR_V))
        self.play(Indicate(formula[2], color=COLOR_A))
        self.play(Indicate(formula[1], color=COLOR_B))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Conveyor belt visuals
        belt = Line(self.grid['D6'], self.grid['D1'], color=GRAY_A, stroke_width=2)
        
        machine_a_box = Square(side_length=0.8, color=COLOR_A, fill_opacity=0.2)
        label_a = Text("A", color=COLOR_A, font_size=24).move_to(machine_a_box)
        machine_a = VGroup(machine_a_box, label_a)
        self.place_at_grid(machine_a, 'D4')
        
        machine_b_box = Square(side_length=0.8, color=COLOR_B, fill_opacity=0.2)
        label_b = Text("B", color=COLOR_B, font_size=24).move_to(machine_b_box)
        machine_b = VGroup(machine_b_box, label_b)
        self.place_at_grid(machine_b, 'D2')
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        vector_v = Text("v", color=COLOR_V, font_size=36, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_v, 'D6')
        
        self.play(Create(belt))
        self.play(FadeIn(machine_a), FadeIn(machine_b))
        self.play(FadeIn(vector_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_V))
        
        # Vector v enters machine A then machine B
        self.play(vector_v.animate.move_to(self.grid['D4']), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(machine_a, color=WHITE))
        self.play(vector_v.animate.move_to(self.grid['D2']), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(machine_b, color=WHITE))
        self.play(vector_v.animate.move_to(self.grid['D1']), run_time=1)
        
        # Right-to-Left Label and Arrows
        arrow_flow = Arrow(start=self.grid['E5'], end=self.grid['E2'], color=COLOR_V, buff=0.1)
        label_flow = Text("Right-to-Left Order", color=COLOR_V, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(label_flow, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_flow), Write(label_flow))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    """
    Fixed implementation for Section 6.
    Class renamed to 'Section6Scene' as required.
    Avoids FileNotFoundError: 'latex' by using Text mobjects for matrices and labels
    instead of TeX-dependent mobjects like IntegerMatrix or MathTex.
    """
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=BLUE_A).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Sidebar content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Right-side visual grid reference points
        self.grid_center = RIGHT * 3

    def create_text_matrix(self, data, color=WHITE):
        """
        Creates a matrix representation using only Text mobjects
        to bypass the requirement for a LaTeX installation.
        """
        # Create matrix elements as Text
        matrix_rows = []
        for row_data in data:
            row_group = VGroup(*[
                Text(str(item), font_size=24, color=color) for item in row_data
            ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
            matrix_rows.append(row_group)
        
        # Arrange rows vertically
        matrix_content = VGroup(*matrix_rows).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        
        # Create brackets using Text or Lines
        bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=48, color=color).next_to(matrix_content, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=48, color=color).next_to(matrix_content, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        return VGroup(bracket_l, matrix_content, bracket_r)

    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        self.setup_layout(
            "Section 6: Linear Transformations",
            ["• Basis Vectors", "• Matrix Multiplication", "• Coordinate Mapping"]
        )

        # Example Matrix Data
        data = [[3, 1], [0, 2]]
        matrix_mobj = self.create_text_matrix(data)
        matrix_mobj.move_to(self.grid_center)

        # Labels for the matrix
        label = Text("Transformation Matrix A:", font_size=24).next_to(matrix_mobj, UP, buff=0.5)

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_mobj))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Show an update to the matrix to demonstrate functionality
        new_data = [[1, 0], [0, 1]]
        new_matrix = self.create_text_matrix(new_data, color=YELLOW)
        new_matrix.move_to(self.grid_center)
        
        self.play(Transform(matrix_mobj, new_matrix))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication: The Art of Composition
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Matrix as a Movement
sections.content: Briefly revisit the idea that a matrix acts as a function on space. Visualize a 2D grid and a 'Geometry Robot' character. When we multiply a vector by Matrix A, the Robot moves (rotates, scales, or shears). Emphasize that the columns of the matrix show where the basis vectors (i and j) land.
sections.example: A 90-degree rotation matrix A transforms the Robot standing at (1,0) to the position (0,1).

sections.title: The Sequential Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the scenario of applying two transformations in a row. First, the Robot is transformed by Matrix A (Rotation), and then the result is transformed by Matrix B (Shear). Show the intermediate step where the Robot stops briefly before the second movement.
sections.example: Robot first rotates 90 degrees (A), then is stretched horizontally by a factor of 2 (B). We track its path from start to middle to finish.

sections.title: Defining the 'Shortcut' (The Product)
sections.content: Explain that Matrix Multiplication is simply finding a 'single' matrix (C) that performs both movements in one leap. This 'Master Matrix' C is the product BA. Graphically show the 'intermediate' grid disappearing as the Robot 'teleports' directly from its initial state to the final state.
sections.example: Mathematically, instead of B(A(v)), we calculate (BA)v. Matrix C = BA is the consolidated 'instruction manual' for the entire journey.

sections.title: The Right-to-Left Rule
sections.content: Explain the notation convention. In the expression BA, Matrix A acts first because it is closest to the vector. Use the analogy of a 'Function Factory' or 'Layers of an Onion' where the innermost action happens first.
sections.example: Visualizing a conveyor belt: The Robot (Vector) enters from the right, hits Machine A first, then Machine B. Therefore, we write the combined operation as B times A.

sections.title: Why Order Matters (Non-Commutativity)
sections.content: Demonstrate visually that AB is not the same as BA. Changing the sequence of transformations leads to different destinations. This explains why matrix multiplication isn't like multiplying regular numbers.
sections.example: Compare: (1) Rotate then Slide vs (2) Slide then Rotate. Show two different Robots landing in completely different spots on the grid to emphasize that BA ≠ AB.

sections.title: Summary: The DNA of Transformation
sections.content: Conclude by reinforcing that every time the student sees matrix multiplication, they should see a 'composition of actions'. Summarize the flow: Vector -> First Action -> Second Action = Product Matrix.
sections.example: A final high-speed animation showing complex patterns (like a kaleidoscope) being controlled by a single product of three different transformation matrices.
